videos.title: How a Circle works
videos.description: A short introduction to reading, respectful disagreement and sharing with care. Original silent SoE video with captions.
videos.credit: Original Society of Explorers text and canvas graphics. No third-party media, audio, music or voice.
videos.transcript:
How a Circle works
Read. Reflect. Share.
A good conversation starts with a good question.

Choose a Circle
Find a time and place that work for you.
Read the source before your meeting.

Bring your perspective
Christian and conservative roots.
Every faith and view is welcome.

Make room for disagreement
Challenge an idea.
Treat the person with respect.

Share with care
Keep other members’ words private.
Ask before recording.

Start with the reading
Find a Circle. Read.
Join the conversation.

videos.title: Who gets the night sky?
videos.description: The Archivist looks at actual 2026 footage from Paranal, Chile, and asks how we should weigh satellite internet against a shared night sky. A silent 24-second Reel.

attribution.edits: Trimmed, framed vertically and annotated with AI-assisted commentary. Source audio omitted.

videos.transcript:
The night sky has traffic. A time-lapse
excerpt from Paranal, Chile, filmed May 19,
2026.

A lifeline far from a tower. Satellite
internet can connect places beyond ground
networks.

A cost for the telescope. Bright trails can
obscure part of a telescope image.

Who gets the night sky? What brightness
limit would you set? Bring your reason to a
Circle.
